summary.headline: IndoStar Q1 FY27 PAT rebounded to INR11 crore from a INR424 crore loss in Q4 FY26, as credit cost fell to INR81.4 crore and disbursements rose 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore.
summary.overview:
Disbursements grew 44% YoY to INR1,235 crore, though slightly lower QoQ, and AUM reached INR8,244 crore (up 2% QoQ, 6% YoY). Net interest income rose 39% YoY to about INR219 crore and NIM expanded to 8.8% from 6.2%. Impairment charge fell sharply to INR81.4 crore from INR517.3 crore in Q4, which had included one-time SR and management overlay provisions, lifting PAT to INR11 crore. Management expects the old pre-Jan 2025 book to run off over 2 to 3 quarters, driving lower GNPA and credit cost.</overview>

segments.name: Vehicle finance
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR1,185 crore (+43% YoY from INR831 crore), disbursement yield 17.4% (vs 17.2% in Q4); AUM INR7,724 crore. Cars now 21% of AUM (17% a year ago), M&HCV 35% (42%), small LCV 21% (25%), construction equipment 10% (8%), farm 6% (5%).

segments.name: Micro LAP
segments.commentary: Disbursements INR50 crore (+85% YoY from INR27 crore); yield 21.4%; AUM INR217 crore (+24% QoQ, ~3x YoY). GNPA 0.17%, 90+ DPD 0.17%; average ticket size up from INR5.9 lakh to ~INR8.2 lakh over the year; 125 co-located branches (108 last quarter).

guidance_outlook: Disbursement growth of 35% CAGR over 3 years targeted; Q1 at 44% YoY, and management expects 35%+ YoY in Q2 based on July trend.
FY29 target of PAT INR450-500 crore reiterated; management says PPOP growth is in place and PAT growth will follow over the next 2-3 quarters as credit cost falls.

Disbursement yield to hold around 17-17.25% per quarter; cost of borrowing expected to decline as a high-cost tranche (about INR250 crore at ~12-13%) matures in Q2, converging toward ~9% by March 2027.
Old (pre-Jan 2025) book share of AUM to rise from 60% (Mar 2026) to 68% (Jun 2026) and about 85% by Q4 FY27 as the new book grows.
Micro LAP AUM to double in FY27; UP and Bihar launches in August and September; long-term Micro LAP mix target of 15-20% of AUM over 3-5 years.
Sales headcount to be about 50% higher by March 2027 vs March 2026; branch network 468 now, target above 500 this year.
INR49 crore management overlay (West Asia) retained; release depends on portfolio performance and macro.
capex_capacity: Branch network at 468 across 24 states and UTs after adding 14 branches in the quarter; target to cross 500 this year.
Micro LAP operates from 125 co-located branches (108 last quarter) in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Gujarat, with no incremental branch capex.
Field sales force up about 30% in the last six months; target of about 50% higher by March 2027 vs March 2026.
Login-to-disbursement TAT in vehicle finance down 44% over the last year through digitisation and loan simplification.

Liquidity: total liquidity INR586 crore, INR235 crore above policy minimum; average excess liquidity INR529 crore in the quarter, held as a buffer against West Asia risk and system tightness, costing about INR8 crore of negative carry.
demand_pricing: Management says competitive intensity is low in Tier 3 to Tier 6 and semi-urban/rural areas; origination at ~20% yield, LTV below 40%, and 95%+ self-occupied residential property.
Passenger car disbursements now exceed M&HCV volumes; M&HCV was muted in the last 1-2 quarters as customers delayed purchases over prices and fuel availability.
Industry: ICRA expects CV wholesale volumes to grow 4-6% in FY27; CRISIL sees used vehicle finance as a key NBFC growth driver.
Collection efficiency about 95%; early delinquency ratio 2.29% (5.55% a year ago); non-starter ratio 1.65% (3.76% a year ago), both up marginally QoQ on seasonality.
Share of customers with CIBIL above 725 at 84% (79% in FY26, 63% in FY24); new-to-credit share 4% (13% in FY24).
